subject: Service disruption: EU & APAC ingress degradation — temporary guidance
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tim Lee <tim.lee@acme.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Service disruption: EU & APAC ingress degradation — temporary guidance

Hi Tim / ACME ops team,

Quick update from Redwood: between ~08:40–09:05 UTC we observed an external cloud peering degradation affecting ingress to our EU and APAC front doors. The issues are with the cloud provider’s peering fabric and they are working on a fix; our mitigation engineers have implemented a temporary traffic steering policy but some customers routed to EU/APAC are seeing increased connection errors and longer handshake times.

What you’ll see:
- Intermittent 502/504 responses and TLS handshake timeouts when requests are routed to eu-1 or apac-1 front doors.
- A subset of sessions will reconnect successfully after a retry.

Immediate recommended actions (minimal change, low risk):
1) If you have region hints in your integration, set region=us (or remove region pinning) to prefer the US front door for the short term.
2) Increase client-side retry to 2 attempts with exponential backoff (200ms -> 800ms) for generation/streaming endpoints.
3) If you rely on a fixed IP allowlist, add the US ingress CIDR: 203.0.113.0/24 temporarily.

We attached a short fallback runbook with CLI steps and example curl commands (eu-apac-fallback-runbook.pdf). I’ve also included a concise reconnect checklist (reconnect-checklist.txt) for your SREs.

Data residency note: routing to the US front door will not change your stored data location for model logs/metrics — we are only changing ingress path. If you have strict residency restrictions, reply and I’ll escalate to our compliance team immediately.

ETA: provider reports a patching window of 2–3 hours; we’ll update you every 30 minutes or as soon as we have meaningful changes.

Call option: if you want a quick runthrough with our infra team now, I can join with Vivek.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0142

--Attachment: eu-apac-fallback-runbook.pdf (PDF, 180KB)
--Attachment: reconnect-checklist.txt (TXT, 1.2KB)
From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@acme.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:46:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Service disruption: EU & APAC ingress degradation — temporary guidance

Thanks Marissa — appreciated. A couple quick clarifications:
- If we switch region=us for requests, will request latency for our EU users spike above our SLA? We need to understand 95th percentile impact.
- Our security team flagged the temporary IP change — is 203.0.113.0/24 the only CIDR we need to add?
- We have a compliance clause that prohibits EU traffic leaving the region for certain models. If we route to US, does that violate that clause?

If needed I can loop in procurement/security — we may need an exec note if data residency is at risk.

Tim
Head of Platform Engineering, ACME, Inc.
ops@acme.io | +44 20 7946 0821

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tim Lee <tim.lee@acme.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Service disruption: EU & APAC ingress degradation — temporary guidance

Hi Tim — quick answers below, and happy to hop on a call if you prefer.

1) Latency impact: routing to the US front door typically adds 30–70ms median for EU-origin traffic and 95th percentile can increase more depending on network path. For most lightweight generation calls this stays within typical SLA bounds; for latency-sensitive streaming we recommend keep-alive + smaller chunk windows and the retry guidance above. I’ve attached an internal 95th% impact sketch in the runbook.

2) IP allowlist: yes, 203.0.113.0/24 is the primary US ingress prefix we are switching to for impacted customers. We also published a short-lived alternate at 198.51.100.0/26 as a backup; both are listed in the runbook.

3) Data residency: switching ingress does not move stored logs/backups or model artifacts. For customers with contractual residency restrictions on specific model outputs, we will not automatically route requests to a different jurisdiction — I’ll escalate your account to Compliance immediately for an exception evaluation. If this is high risk for you, we will keep traffic to EU only and instead enable queuing/fallback at the application level until the provider stabilization completes.

Proposed next steps:
- If you can accept the temporary ingress change, add the CIDR and flip region=us for the next 30–90 minutes. We’ll monitor and revert as soon as the provider confirms stable peering.
- If you need us to keep traffic in-region, reply and we’ll coordinate a no-exit plan + explicit SLA credit request.

Call: Vivek and I are available at 10:30 UTC for a short screenshare.

Thanks — we’ll keep this thread updated every 30 minutes.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 16:38:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: ACME — post-incident follow-up & action items (EU/APAC ingress)

Folks — logging an internal summary for ACME after today’s ingress degradation. They accepted the temporary US ingress and flipped region hints; we saw drop in errors by ~92% within 12 minutes. Provider confirmed full peering restoration at 15:04 UTC. Customer asked for a formal postmortem and an assessment of residency exposure.

Action items:
- Vivek: produce a short technical RCA (root cause + timeline) and include network-level traces from 08:30–15:30 UTC. Target: draft by 2026-07-30 18:00 UTC.
- Laura: lead the compliance assessment for ACME’s contract clause re: jurisdictional data movement; if an exception was effectively required, prepare a one-page exec note for CS/legal. Target: 2026-07-31 12:00 UTC.
- Marissa (me): prepare customer-facing postmortem (high-level timeline, mitigation steps we took, and remediation plan). I’ll draft and send to ACME by 2026-07-29 11:00 UTC and include the runbook and test checklist.

Attached: final versions of the fallback runbook we used and a short reconnect checklist for ACME’s SREs. I’ll also link the provider incident page and our internal incident record in the postmortem.

Notes: the customer asked about SLA credit language — I’ll coordinate with revenue ops if they request a formal credit. Also recommend we add a short synthetic test that alerts on peering-health degradation (Vivek to scope).

Thanks,
Marissa
